subject.title: iOS app: node requests re-approval on every reconnect (token persistence bug)

question: Should iOS node reconnects treat volatile permission and watch-reachability changes as non-approval metadata, or should the gateway continue requiring reapproval for every declared permission-surface change?
rationale: The remaining plausible cause is not just token storage; it is the security boundary between harmless mobile state drift and approval-worthy node capability changes, which needs maintainer intent plus live iOS proof.

options.title: Prove And Narrow Volatile Metadata
options.body: Run the current-main iOS reconnect scenario and, if confirmed, adjust only volatile iOS permission/watch fields so stable approved capabilities do not require reapproval on every reconnect.

options.title: Keep Strict Reapproval
options.body: Leave the current gateway policy intact and document that permission/watch state changes intentionally require approval even if it causes repeated iOS prompts.

options.title: Close As Partially Fixed
options.body: Close only if a maintainer accepts the LAN bootstrap and per-gateway credential fixes as sufficient without a fresh live iOS reproduction.

recommendation.title: Prove And Narrow Volatile Metadata
recommendation.body: Run the current-main iOS reconnect scenario and, if confirmed, adjust only volatile iOS permission/watch fields so stable approved capabilities do not require reapproval on every reconnect.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the latest iOS gateway credential/state work and is the best available owner for the mobile auth/security boundary decision.
